editorial:
You know that feeling when your kid brings home someone you just can't stand? That's the whole setup here, and it's played for big laughs. A protective dad visits his daughter at college and meets her boyfriend, a wealthy tech guy who is loud, tattooed, and completely clueless about boundaries. The two men clash right away, and the movie rides that tension through a series of awkward dinners, embarrassing moments, and over-the-top gestures. Bryan Cranston is great as the uptight father, and James Franco leans fully into the goofy rich guy role. The humor is crude and silly, so if you enjoy that kind of comedy, you'll have a good time. The pacing stays quick, and there are enough funny set pieces to keep you entertained from start to finish.

On the downside, the jokes can feel repetitive, and some scenes push too hard for shock value. Still, the heart of the story is about a dad learning to let go, which gives it a sweet center beneath all the chaos. If you want a light, dumb-fun movie night with friends, this is a solid pick. Stream it in 4K Ultra HD on Prime Video, rent it on Apple TV, or grab the 4K Blu-ray for your collection.
endingExplained: In the final scenes, the dad finally accepts the boyfriend after seeing how much he truly loves his daughter. The boyfriend proposes during a big holiday party, and the dad, despite his earlier hatred, gives his blessing. The movie ends with the family coming together, showing that even the most unlikely pair can find common ground when love is involved.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves awkward family comedies and crude humor.
